AFWD.chosen_element: finite-N enumeration and Monte Carlo generation, transforming a walk configuration into its end-to-end distance, then averaging over many walks to produce a mean-square displacement R^2(N)
AFWD.justification: forward morphism carrying the raw walk space into a concrete measurable quantity, advancing toward the exponent

AREV.chosen_element: the attempt to pass to the limit N→∞, which cannot be executed by any finite algorithm because the walk length diverges
AREV.justification: descent morphism: the ideal infinite limit is not constructively reachable from the finite realizations, representing a downward movement toward impossibility

CLINK.chosen_element: the pipeline connecting the displacement computation to the power-law fit, chaining the extraction of the exponent ν from the log-log slope of R^2(N)
CLINK.justification: composition of the forward transformation with the regression step; without this link the exponent remains unreadable

ENGAGR.chosen_element: the live contradiction of holding a sharp estimate and the impossibility of exact knowledge in the same system, without resolving one away
ENGAGR.justification: paraconsistent holding of both the true (approximate) and false (exact) states together as B — the real epistemic state of the problem

EVALF.chosen_element: the proof that no finite algorithm can decide the exact asymptotic exponent, because any finite N leaves open infinitely many possible growths
EVALF.justification: negative arm: the constructively refuted possibility that the exact ν is algorithmically attainable, rendering the infinite limit an unreachable falsehood

EVALT.chosen_element: the convergent finite‑N fit yielding a constructive estimate ν_finite, supported by error bars and consistency across methods
EVALT.justification: affirmative arm: the constructive truth that a finite numerical exponent can be computed and is not refuted

FFUSE.chosen_element: the conjunction of a numerical estimate ν ≈ 0.5876 (finite arm) and the demonstration that no finite procedure can fix the exact value (infinite arm)
FFUSE.justification: multiplication rejoining the contradictory arms into a single resolved state where both hold together — the exponent is simultaneously approximately known and exactly unknown

FSPLIT.chosen_element: the methodological fork: one arm operates on finite realizations, the other arm addresses the unattainable infinite limit
FSPLIT.justification: co‑multiplication that separates the computable finite‑N regime from the ideal N→∞ regime, each branch taking a different path

IFIX.chosen_element: the published record in the corpus stating the current bounds: 0.5 < ν < 1 in general dimensions, with numerical estimates stored as appendices
IFIX.justification: irreversible fixation: once the bound is committed to the literature, it cannot be unwritten; future work builds upon it

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: ν itself as a self‑similar scaling parameter, defined by the property that R^2(N) ∼ const · N^{2ν} for large N
IMSCRIB.justification: identity: the exponent is its own reference; recognizing it as the object of study does not alter the state

TANCH.chosen_element: the closed problem statement: the exact value of ν is unknown but its range is bounded by 0.5 < ν ≤ 1, recorded in the consensus literature
TANCH.justification: the terminal anchor that contains the entire investigation, sealing the system with the open question

VINIT.chosen_element: raw ensemble of self-avoiding walks on a d-dimensional lattice, no step count selected, no coordinate measured
VINIT.justification: the void before any displacement is computed, before any walk is instantiated; the state where ν is not yet approached

phase_2.fuse_element: the conjunction of the finite estimate and the unreachability proof
phase_2.fuse_result: a single B state: the exponent ν is constructively estimated (T) and constructively unknowable exactly (F) — both held, not resolved to a single classical value
phase_2.rejoin_note: branch A performs AFWD and a power-law fit (CLINK → EVALT) to produce a numerical ν; branch B applies AREV to reach the impossibility result (CLINK → EVALF). They rejoin via FFUSE, producing the paraconsistent B, and then ENGAGR explicitly holds that contradiction. The fork closes because both arms feed the same terminal anchor.
phase_2.split_input: the unmeasured ensemble of self-avoiding walks before any length is selected
split_outputs: branch A: finite‑N arm where walks are actually generated and measured
branch B: infinite‑limit arm where the exact asymptotic exponent is shown unreachable
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — the paraconsistent resolution: ν is known approximately and simultaneously not knowable exactly; the contradiction is the final verdict
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — the constructive refutation that ν can be determined exactly by any finite procedure
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — a constructive finite‑N estimate of ν, proven to hold within its error bounds
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — the state before any walk is instantiated; no length, no displacement, no ν

steps.domain_action: the raw space of all possible SAW configurations in d dimensions, no length N assigned, no metric computed
define ν as the self‑similar scaling of mean‑square displacement; the identity of the exponent is recognized
split the search for ν into two arms: the finite‑computation arm (A) and the ideal infinite‑limit arm (B)
on arm A, transform a walk of length N into its end‑to‑end distance; average over many walks to obtain R^2(N)
chain the measured R^2(N) to a log‑log regression that extracts the exponent from the asymptotic law
arm A succeeds — a constructive estimate ν_finite is produced with known confidence
on arm B, descend from the finite walks to the unreachable N→∞ limit; no algorithm can complete this passage
connect the descent to the demonstration that exact ν cannot be algorithmically decided
arm B refutes the attainable exact value — the limit is constructively false as a computable object
rejoin the two arms; the finite estimate (T) and the impossibility of exact knowledge (F) fuse into a single B state
hold both the approximate knowledge and the exact ignorance together as a live contradiction, without resolution
record the fused contradictory state — the numerical estimate and the proof of undecidability — as the current scientific consensus, permanently appended
the system closes; the growth exponent remains bounded but unfixed, contained within the anchored open problem

phase_5.alfs_store: the bootstrap corpus of known SAW exponents, the Flory formula, and the rigorous bounds from Madras–Slade and Clisby–Dunweg
phase_5.compiler_frontend: the simulation suite that translates a lattice type, dimension, and walk length into an SAW generation algorithm
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: shared-memory buffers and file-based interchange between the walk generator, displacement aggregator, and the curve-fitting module
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the list of visited lattice sites for each walk, the accumulated sum of squared distances, and the cache of log‑log regression matrices
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: a sequential loop over N values, stepping from short to longer walks to cover the scaling window, with Monte Carlo repetitions at each length

phase_6.cycle_cost: CPU cycles per sampled walk, memory writes for displacement accumulation, and regression matrix operations
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the net information about ν, from complete ignorance to a bounded paraconsistent holding, is conserved through the constructive process; no bit is lost, only structured into contradiction
phase_6.post_cycle_state: a B state of conflicting estimates and impossibility, recorded permanently; the range of possible ν is narrowed but not collapsed
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: the unmeasured SAW ensemble — no exponent data exists, uncertainty maximal
